notes:
- Windows: TMPlayer starts again on computers where it closed at once with "failedChats must not be null"
- Desktop Home: one starred chat is enough for the carousel, and the rows no longer jump while Home fills in
- Casting: subtitles show on the TV, and a soundtrack the TV cannot play is converted on the phone so it is heard, with its audio and subtitle choices kept
- Casting: the device list stays open and says it is connecting until the TV is ready, and a 4K video on a 1080p TV says so instead of failing
- Casting: if the connection to the TV drops, the video waits with Reconnect and Play here instead of starting on the phone, and a short pause from Telegram is retried
- The update window shows what changed as a list, on phone, TV and desktop
- On a phone, the screen shown when a video stops arriving fits sideways and upright

- Android TV: a new top bar in place of the side rail. Your profile, Search, Home, Chats and Settings along the top, the pages at full width, Up and Down between the bar and the page, and Back to reach the bar from anywhere
- Cast to a Chromecast or Google TV from the phone and the desktop, with the controls staying on your device: MKV videos play without stalling, audio tracks switch on the TV, and your place follows you back to the phone
- Connecting to Telegram never waits in silence: a live status line, and when it takes too long the likely reason with Retry, Use a proxy and Send logs, on phone, TV and desktop
- Proxies (MTProto, SOCKS5, HTTP or a t.me/proxy link), before sign in and from Settings, for networks where Telegram is blocked; sign in with an email code works too
- Search across all your chats, with one result per video and filters, and find a person, group or channel by @username; tap a chat's name for its picture, username, description and link
- t.me links open in TMPlayer: a post plays from its start time, a public chat or an invite shows before you join
- Telegram's own lighter copies of a big video (720p, 480p) to pick from, picked for you on a slow line, with Telegram's seek previews and the uploader's cover
- A video posted more than once is one card: pick the copy and quality, and your place follows it. A video cut into .part001 pieces plays as one
- Home opens on a calmer carousel of the newest videos, and Home appears ready rather than filling in
- Player: chapters, picture shape on the bar, finer speed steps, Night mode for quieter loud scenes, a way back after a long jump, and subtitles at the same height on every video
- Appearance: a Pure black switch for OLED screens that also follows the system's dark mode, and nine accent colours
- Connected devices: where TMPlayer is signed in, and ending those sessions without signing out Telegram's own apps
- Storage at a glance in a chart, everything on the device listed, Free up space with Low storage mode, and Low storage mode keeping to its limit
- Notifications for new episodes of shows you watch, finished downloads, low storage and updates, each with its own switch
- Videos in a post's comments, round videos, Forward to a chat, Save to the gallery, an Audio list per chat, and resume on your other devices through your Saved Messages (opt in)
- macOS: sign in works on Macs without Homebrew, and a new installer window. Windows: an update keeps TMPlayer and your sign in
- Many fixes on phone, TV and desktop, in all 21 languages

- A new Home with posters, overviews and episode names for films and shows, and TMPlayer rows on the Android TV home screen
- A setup and a quick tour after sign in, in every language, with Performance and Mobile data steps; existing users are offered the tour once
- Low storage mode streams videos larger than the free space, and Save mobile data fetches only a few minutes ahead on mobile data
- Skip intro, recap and credits, speed remembered per series, preferred audio and subtitle language, watch later, season downloads, bookmarks, A-B repeat and skip silence
- Backups of settings and lists, an app PIN and a kids lock with allowed chats
- After a crash, TMPlayer asks before sending a report, once or always
- A macOS preview for Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 26 or newer
- New icons, the desktop's own window buttons, and many fixes for right-to-left languages, TV focus and long translations

Series now have an Episodes list in the player on phone, TV and desktop, with autoplay to the next episode and marking episodes watched right from the list. The side bar is simpler: Home, History, Favourites, Chats, Downloads and Settings, and Only my folders hides Telegram's own Chats and Saved groups. There is a shorter welcome tour, and Home says how to get a first video in. TMPlayer now asks before forgetting progress, clearing caches or deleting downloads. On desktop, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Bengali, Malayalam, Arabic and Persian show even without system fonts, and the AppImage updates only what changed. On TV, OK pauses in one press and See all sits on each Home row. Labels that were cut short in German, Russian and Malayalam fit, and buttons in the light theme are readable again.

TMPlayer now speaks 21 languages (machine translated for now, corrections welcome on GitHub). Home has rows, series get their own page, and search covers all your chats. Optional posters and overviews come from TMDB, TVmaze and AniList, and subtitles can be found online through OpenSubtitles. The player adds volume boost, a sleep timer, a "still watching?" check, subtitle and audio delay, subtitle size and position, and simpler controls on phone, TV and desktop. Downloads can be removed after watching. On TV: Fire TV remotes, Watch Next and seek previews. On desktop the QR sign in works in release builds, and there is a new About screen everywhere.
Videos play on Android TV again. In 1.22.0 the player closed itself a few seconds into every video on a television; phones and computers were not affected.
Smaller downloads. The Android APK is about half its old size, and the Windows and Linux packages are a third to almost two thirds smaller. The Linux tarball is now a .tar.xz.

Finished episodes now get a tick, and any video can be marked as watched or unwatched by hand. A new Watched tab lists what you have finished. Searching a chat now finds videos outside the size limits, and the grid says how many videos the limits are hiding. On a TV, the release page opens as a QR code. On Windows, the media keys and the media flyout control the player.
The first release with a desktop app for Windows and Linux. It signs in with the same Telegram account and plays the same chats, with the keyboard, the mouse and your media keys.
